text: The previous trading day's high is considered and a zone is drawn (author: "the high should be considered, day's high should be considered and a zone should be drawn").
Wick should be ignored, but body should be considered: a price that is only a wick is ignored; a body high is considered when drawing the zone.
implemented_by: body_high(); zone ceiling = highest body high
supersedes: PDR guide p.2 'upper boundary: the highest point of the upper wick';PDR-A01 (Phase 3.4: ceiling = wick high)

text: Reading of B01a: for every completed previous-session 5-minute candle body_high = max(open, close); the principal reference is the highest body_high; the wick-only high is never the active ceiling (it is kept as a diagnostic).
source: Phase 3.6 brief interpretation of the author's words

text: If there are multiple highs, a zone that connects all of them is considered (principle only; the author gave no numbers).
How many body highs make 'multiple': distinct touch groups >= b_min_touches (default 2).
Maximum difference between body highs: a body-high pivot within b_tolerance_points (default 5.0) of the highest body high joins the cluster.
Minimum candle separation: members closer than b_min_separation_candles (default 2) count as one touch.
What counts as a body high of the cluster: a body-high pivot not lower than its b_local_high_k (default 1) neighbours on each side (non-strict).
A lone body spike above repeated body highs is never discarded (ALWAYS_INCLUDE_HIGHEST_BODY_HIGH); excluding it is a diagnostic option only. A wick-only spike is ignored by B01a, not by this policy.

Lower boundary: the zone is the hull of the member candles' bodies - floor = the lowest body_low among the members; for candidate A the member is the highest-body-high candle alone, so the floor is its body low. The author gave no lower-boundary rule.
Equal highest body highs: the first candle anchors the zone.

A zone with zero height (ceiling == floor) is detected and flagged ZERO_HEIGHT_ZONE; by default the setup is left UNRESOLVED (no signal) instead of inventing a width; TREAT_AS_LINE is a sensitivity option.

The next session's opening price must be strictly above the previous day's resistance-zone ceiling (session_open > zone_upper); an open inside the zone, below it or exactly at the ceiling rejects the setup.
The next day must also open gap up (open above the official previous close).
source: PDR_Strategy_Guide.pdf p.1 'Market must open gap up'

text: Price must return to / interact with the zone (any candle whose range overlaps the zone +/- proximity) before the confirmation candle; the confirmation comes strictly after the test candle.
A LONG entry needs one good green body candle OR a lower price rejection candle OR a hammer candle.
Fixed body-percentage and wick-size thresholds are not required by the author.
Reading of B04: OR logic; every pattern that passes is recorded; one signal per candle; rejection and hammer need no particular colour.
source: Phase 3.6 brief interpretation of the author's words

text: A deterministic research classification is unavoidable: profile RESEARCH_DEFAULT (carried from Phase 3.5 for comparability: good green body = bullish, body >= 60% and upper wick <= 20% of the range; rejection = lower wick >= 2x body, close in the top 30% of the range, low reached the zone ceiling; hammer = lower wick >= 2x body, upper wick <= 10%, body bottom at >= 60% of the range). NOT author-approved; chosen neither by profit nor by journal agreement.
The confirmation candle should close above the zone.
Reading of B05: close > the zone CEILING, strictly; equal, inside the zone or below the floor is invalid; a lower wick may penetrate the zone.
source: Phase 3.6 brief interpretation of the author's words

text: Entry only after the confirmation candle has completed; fill = open of the 1-minute bar that starts when it ends (existing EXE-FILL-001 convention).
The test stays armed until a candle qualifies or the session ends (wait_policy); the confirmation may not be the test candle (preserved legacy rule).
